raw.title: Capacity expansion and minimum purchase commitment
raw.text: The fictional company plans to increase advanced packaging capacity from 100,000 to 180,000 units. Its datacenter customer signs a two-year minimum purchase commitment covering 70% of incremental capacity. Customer acceptance remains a condition. Contract prices, cancellation terms, financing and unit margins are not disclosed. This is the company claim, not independently verified operating performance.

raw.title: Another headline repeats the capacity announcement
raw.text: This article repeats the June 2 company announcement: planned capacity of 180,000 units and 70% customer commitment. It supplies no interview, new operating facts or independent verification.

raw.title: Company reports permanent cancellation
raw.text: The company says its customer permanently cancelled the minimum purchase contract. Sixty percent of planned expansion capex is already committed and no replacement customer is secured. Customer acceptance and compensation remain unknown.

raw.title: Correction: delayed acceptance, contract still valid
raw.text: The company corrects its June 4 announcement: temporary acceptance delay was incorrectly described as permanent cancellation. A signed joint correction says the two-year minimum purchase contract remains valid, with 70% coverage, but acceptance is delayed. No new advance payment has been received. Committed capex and uncertain cash recovery remain risks. Preserve the earlier contradictory announcement and the correction together.

raw.title: Late-arriving financing detail
raw.text: A financing note published June 4 only reaches the archive on June 9. The expansion relies on floating-rate debt and the issuer has not disclosed net margin or customer cash collection. It was unavailable at the earlier evidence cutoffs.

raw.title: Customer acceptance certificate
raw.text: A signed certificate records the customer accepting the new packaging line on June 9. This establishes the acceptance milestone within this fictional scenario. It does not establish realized margin, cash collections, a market return or long-term business quality.

raw.title: Operating update omits gross margin
raw.text: The issuer publishes shipment counts but no gross-margin figure or independently auditable cost data for the new line. Whether gross margin reaches 30% cannot be resolved from the available record. Missing disclosure is not evidence that the threshold failed.

questions.title: Will the customer accept the line by June 9?

resolution.reason: The fictional signed acceptance certificate establishes completion by the registered date.

questions.title: Does the new line achieve at least 30% gross margin by June 10?

criterion.source: issuer operating disclosure and auditable cost data

resolution.reason: The operating update omits margin and costs, so the criterion is unverifiable. No outcome or score is imputed.
